interpretation.summary: A Pearson correlation was computed to assess the linear association between x and y using 19 complete observations. The estimated correlation was 0.99174, with a ninety-five percent confidence interval from 0.97815 to 0.99689, and the associated p-value was 1.3179e-16. Because the p-value is below the five percent threshold, the result is classified as evidence of a linear association. The positive direction indicates that higher values of x tend to accompany higher values of y, but this reflects association only and not a causal relationship. One observation was excluded through complete-case deletion, so the analysis reflects only records with non-missing values on both variables.
limitations: Pearson correlation captures linear association only; nonlinear relationships may be missed.
